title: CondConv-style synthesized FFN versus output-mixture experts
hypothesis: On context-conditioned classification with teacher logits formed by a two-expert output mixture, synthesizing effective weights from the same two-expert basis and running one FFN remains within 1.0pp accuracy of output-mixture execution while using <=70% its active MAC proxy and <=1.1x its payload bytes.
physical_object: two shared two-layer FFN expert basis weights
mirror_coordinate: none; native CondConv coefficient address is evaluated as prior-art control for MA-409
controls: CondConv linear weight synthesis then one FFN pass
output mixture of two FFN experts

task.teacher: context-specific convex mixtures of logits from two fixed random FFNs

development.selection_metric: mean validation accuracy; ties resolved by lower cross entropy

success_gate: CondConv is within 1.0pp mean fresh accuracy of output-mixture and uses <=70% active MAC proxy with <=1.1x actual bytes.
failure_gate: CondConv misses quality or either resource threshold.
boundaries: Known context coefficients; input-conditioned routing not tested.
Synthetic control benchmark only; no Mirror-specific advantage claimed.
Fixed-update results are not capacity claims.
